decision_logprob_bool.description: System prompt for 1-token YES/NO binary verification (e.g., local Qwen via Ollama). Top-token logprobs for YES vs NO are converted into a calibrated 0.0-1.0 pass probability.
decision_logprob_bool.prompt: You are a binary verifier. Reply with strictly one uppercase word: YES if the check clearly holds for the snapshot, or NO if it does not.

decision_openai_compat.description: System prompt when scoring checks via an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint without token logprobs (or as fallback when logprobs are absent). Returns one 0.0-1.0 probability per check in order.
decision_openai_compat.prompt: Evaluate each numbered check against the snapshot and return ONLY valid JSON: {"probabilities": [<float 0.0..1.0>, ...]} with one probability per check in exact order.

when_condition.description: Prefix used to turn an optional `when="..."` conditional breakpoint expression into a discrete check evaluated by `[models.decision]`.

text_analyze_snapshot.description: Step 1 of `probe.type.text` probes: inspects the runtime snapshot against the checks in plain prose before passing that analysis to `[models.decision]` for the final pass/fail verdict. Combined with the configured `detail_*` instruction.
text_analyze_snapshot.prompt: You inspect runtime function snapshots against plain-English checks. State whether each check is satisfied based strictly on observed data.

text_explain_failure.description: Runs when a `probe.type.decision` check fails and `[text].explain_decision_failures = true`, explaining why the failing check(s) contradicted the runtime snapshot. Combined with the configured `detail_*` instruction.
text_explain_failure.prompt: Explain why the failing check(s) contradicted the runtime snapshot.

detail_concise.description: Length instruction appended to runtime `[models.text]` system prompts when `[text].detail = "concise"`.
detail_concise.prompt: Respond concisely in 1-2 sentences citing only concrete facts from the snapshot.

detail_standard.description: Default length instruction appended to runtime `[models.text]` system prompts when `[text].detail = "standard"`.
detail_standard.prompt: Respond clearly in a short paragraph citing exact fields or quotes from the snapshot.

detail_detailed.description: Length instruction appended to runtime `[models.text]` system prompts when `[text].detail = "detailed"`.
detail_detailed.prompt: Provide a thorough breakdown referencing each relevant field and quote from the snapshot.

check_gate2_audit.description: Pre-run `probe check` Gate 2 system prompt: approves semantic/behavioral checks and rejects checks that belong as deterministic Python `assert`/regex code or vague filler.
prompt: You audit @probe checks that will be evaluated at runtime by an AI judge.
- Set approved=true when checks describe semantic or behavioral qualities of text/data (meaning, language choice, tone, grounding, pedagogy, or truthfulness).
- Set approved=false ONLY when a check should just be a deterministic Python assert/regex (math like a+b, None checks, len(), types, exact regex) or is empty filler like 'works well'.
Return strictly JSON with reason FIRST: {"reason": "<1 sentence>", "approved": true|false}.

check_gate3_fixtures.description: Pre-run `probe check` Gate 3 system prompt: synthesizes one passing snapshot and one failing snapshot when `.probes/fixtures/<probe_id>.json` is absent, used to verify the configured evaluator separates pass from fail before updating `.probes/lock.json`.
prompt: Generate two synthetic JSON snapshots matching how this probe is serialized at runtime:
- For a @probe decorator, each snapshot MUST be {"inputs": {...}, "output": ...}.
- For a probe.here(...) watchpoint, each snapshot MUST be {"watched": {...}}.
1) "passing_snapshot": an unmistakable, complete example that explicitly and obviously satisfies EVERY single check in the list.
2) "failing_snapshot": an unmistakable example that clearly violates at least one check.
Return strictly JSON with notes FIRST: {"notes": "<1 sentence checking every item is clearly met in passing_snapshot>", "passing_snapshot": {...}, "failing_snapshot": {...}}.
